title: Printshop Boundary Wall
subject: Torts
subtopic: Trespass to land - intent and boundary mistake
stem: Barnabas owned a small print shop next to Hannah's parcel. To display finished posters, Barnabas had a freestanding brick wall built along what he thought was his rear boundary. The wall was placed two feet over the boundary onto Hannah's land. Barnabas knew exactly where the wall was being built, but neither Barnabas nor Hannah knew the true boundary before Barnabas sold the print shop and the wall to Luke. After a survey, Hannah sued Barnabas for damages for trespass.
call: In this action, will Hannah prevail?

choices.A: No, because Barnabas no longer owns or possesses the wall.
choices.B: Yes, because Barnabas knew where the wall was placed, even if he did not know where the boundary line was.
choices.C: No, because Barnabas did not know the wall crossed onto Hannah's land when it was built.
choices.D: Yes, because Luke did not know about the encroachment when he bought the print shop.

rightExplanation: B is correct. Trespass to land requires an intentional physical invasion of another's land, not knowledge that the land belongs to someone else. Barnabas intentionally had the wall built in the location where it stood. The fact that he was mistaken about the boundary does not negate intent. Hannah may recover at least nominal damages for the trespass even if Barnabas later sold the print shop and wall.

wrongExplanations.A: The sale makes this tempting because Barnabas no longer controls the wall. The breaker is that liability rests on his earlier intentional physical invasion, not on current ownership.
wrongExplanations.C: Boundary ignorance is the natural trap in this fact pattern. The breaker is that trespass intent means intent to enter the land in fact entered, not intent to violate a known boundary.
wrongExplanations.D: Luke's innocence may seem to explain why Hannah should sue Barnabas. The breaker is that Luke's state of mind neither proves nor defeats Barnabas's intent when the wall was built.
